metadata.title: Kunskaper, attityder och engagemang i medborgar-, demokrati- och samhällsfrågor hos årskurs 8-elever i ett internationellt perspektiv (ICCS 2022)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICCS 2022 is a two-stage cluster sample in each participating country: schools are sampled first and then one intact class in grade 8 (or grade 9 where age criteria require) is sampled within each selected school; all students in the selected class are included. The report treats ICCS as a survey with sampling uncertainty and uses statistical significance testing at the 5% level when comparing means and proportions across countries, time points, and student subgroups. The excerpted national report does not specify the exact student weight variable names or replicate-weight procedures, but it follows IEA’s guidelines for producing comparable international estimates from the complex design. For analysts using the ICCS international database, the recommended approach is to apply the provided student sampling weights and, where available, replicate weights (or equivalent variance estimation procedures) to obtain correct standard errors and confidence intervals under the complex survey design.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report is a descriptive national results report based on ICCS 2022 achievement scales and questionnaire indices, and it does not present an ML-based predictive modeling pipeline where plausible values (PV) and missing-data handling would need to be explicitly documented for model estimation. The excerpted text describes how ICCS achievement results are placed on a fixed scale and how attitude/engagement indices are constructed, but it does not provide the PV imputation/combining strategy or a missing-data procedure for any statistical model. Therefore, missing-data handling is not reported in the provided material, and the appropriate PV/missing-data details are expected to be documented in the ICCS technical documentation rather than in this national summary.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The target population is students in grade 8 (with a possible shift to grade 9 when the average age is below 13.5). Exclusions follow IEA criteria and can occur at the school level or at the student level: in Sweden, excluded schools include adapted compulsory schools and special schools; students may be excluded for physical or cognitive disabilities that prevent participation, or for being newly arrived in the test language (insufficient Swedish proficiency). In Sweden, 6.4% of the population was excluded (2.1% due to school exclusions and 4.3% due to student exclusions). After exclusions, a two-stage representative sample is drawn within each participating country: schools are sampled randomly and then one intact grade-8 class is sampled within each selected school; all students in the selected class are included. In Sweden, 149 schools participated (97% of the selected schools) and 3263 grade-8 students participated (90% of selected students from those schools), yielding an overall student response rate of 87%.

data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2022 is an international comparative study measuring grade-8 students’ knowledge, attitudes, and engagement in civic, democratic, and societal issues. In this Swedish national report, the authors present descriptive results for Sweden and compare them with the 22 participating countries (with Germany represented only by two federal states). Knowledge is assessed via a rotating test design with about 140 items distributed so that each student answers roughly 35 items, and results are reported on a fixed scale anchored to ICCS 2009 (international mean 500, SD 100). Attitudes and engagement are measured through student questionnaires and summarized using IEA-developed scales/indices, with additional alternative measures based on the proportion agreeing with statements. The report emphasizes that it is not designed to explain causal mechanisms; instead, it documents statistically significant differences (5% level) across countries, time (2009/2016/2022), and student subgroups (gender, socioeconomic background, migration background). It also notes that the COVID-19 period may have affected participation and results differently across countries, and that the report cannot quantify the pandemic’s impact on achievement changes.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a national descriptive results report for ICCS 2022 rather than an empirical machine-learning study. As a result, there is no ML model training, no predictive target variable, and no reported PV-handling or missing-data strategy for an ML estimation pipeline in the provided text. The extraction therefore leaves ML-related fields empty and focuses on survey design, scaling, and subgroup comparisons as the core methodological elements.
